blueprint_concepts: Binomial sums by the differentiation technique (sum of r.C_r, r^2.C_r)
Binomial sums by the integration technique (sum of C_r/(r+1))
english: Let $n$ be a positive integer such that $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{n}\dfrac{\binom{n}{r}}{r+1}=\dfrac{1023}{10}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^{2}\binom{n}{r}$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $n$ एक ऐसा धनात्मक पूर्णांक है कि $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{n}\dfrac{\binom{n}{r}}{r+1}=\dfrac{1023}{10}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^{2}\binom{n}{r}$ बराबर है
solution: $\dfrac{2^{n+1}-1}{n+1}=\dfrac{1023}{10}$ holds for $n=9$, and the left side increases with $n$, so $n=9$
solution_full: Uniqueness: $g(n)=\dfrac{2^{n+1}-1}{n+1}$ satisfies $g(n+1)>g(n)$ for $n\ge1$ (the numerator roughly doubles while the denominator grows by $1$), so $n=9$ is the only solution.
For $\sum r^{2}\binom{n}{r}$: differentiate $(1+x)^{n}$ to get $n(1+x)^{n-1}=\sum r\binom{n}{r}x^{r-1}$; multiply by $x$: $nx(1+x)^{n-1}=\sum r\binom{n}{r}x^{r}$.
(Option (A) is $\sum r(r-1)\binom{9}{r}=9\cdot8\cdot2^{7}$ and option (B) is $\sum r\binom{9}{r}=9\cdot2^{8}$.)
originality_note: New: the index n is recovered from an integration-type sum given only as a number, and then a differentiation-type sum is evaluated (way 5, one sum used to identify the expansion that the other needs). Closest known: evaluate sum C_r/(r+1) or sum r^2 C_r for a given n. Different because: n is not given and must be found by matching (2^(n+1)-1)/(n+1).

concept_use.Binomial sums by the differentiation tec: Sum of r^2 C(n,r) = n(n+1)2^(n-2), obtained by differentiating x(1+x)^(n-1)-type identities twice.
concept_use.Binomial sums by the integration techniq: Sum of C(n,r)/(r+1) = (2^(n+1)-1)/(n+1) by integrating (1+x)^n over [0,1]; it fixes n = 9.

stem_review: Read as a student: n positive integer, the condition fixes n = 9 uniquely (g increasing), summation ranges stated; answer 11520 at option D as planned; options numbers; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Identify n from (2^(n+1)-1)/(n+1) = 1023/10, then the r^2 sum by double differentiation.
justification: Two standard techniques (integration and differentiation of (1+x)^n) linked through an unknown n; each is familiar but the student must run both and match. Placed with the L3 two-ideas-linked anchors such as 2024-P2-Q13 (L3).
